output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a vendor rule update, not by release 6.14. On 3 March at 10:38 UTC Corvane activated a new edge rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks (HTTP 403) password requests that use the nettle-http library and have no edge session cookie. The Android app uses that library for every API call. The first blocks appeared at 10:41. Telemetry shows password success fell from 96% to 8% on every app version and OS version at the same minute. Quick-unlock, iOS and web were unaffected. 6.14 was only at 5% of attempts, and its success matched older versions. Blocked requests came from about 41,300 installed-app IDs, 92% of which had logged in successfully in the previous 90 days, so these are real customers, not bots. Next steps: ask Corvane to set the new rules to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping the other protections on, and confirm recovery in telemetry. Don't roll back 6.14, raise bot sensitivity, or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Excluding them would hide the customer impact. Confidence is high. Contact-centre call volume was probably affected by the fee notices too, so that link is uncertain.
